item.title: Why the UAE deliberately sank 3 ships: Is it good for the ocean’s ecosystem?
item.description: The UAE has strategically sunk three ships, Inchcape 1, 2, and 10, off its east coast to create artificial reefs, fostering marine conservation and ecotourism. These wrecks have transformed into vibrant ecosystems, attracting diverse marine life and divers globally. The initiative demonstrates the UAE's commitment to ecological balance, revitalizing local dive tourism and promoting sustainable diving practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Naming your child in the UAE? This law says you can’t choose just any name
item.description: A viral post has renewed focus on Wadeema’s Law in the UAE, which regulates children’s names to protect dignity and cultural values. Article 8 forbids names that are offensive, humiliating, or clash with religion or customs. The law also ensures every child’s right to registration, nationality, legal parentage, and documentation, placing clear responsibilities on parents or guardians.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US-Syria meeting: Trump holds first-ever White House meeting with Al-Sharaa; America partially waives Caesar Act sanctions — top points
item.description: Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa visited the White House, marking a significant shift as Syria joins the US-led coalition against the Islamic State. The meeting focused on Syria's role in defeating ISIS, reconstruction, and sanctions relief. The US also partially waived Caesar Act sanctions for 180 days, supporting Syria's economic rebuilding efforts.

item.title: Watch: The doctored Trump Jan 6 clip that toppled BBC director-general Tim Davie
item.description: The BBC faces a major controversy after a Panorama documentary aired a doctored clip of Donald Trump's January 6th speech, falsely portraying him as inciting violence. This led to the resignations of top BBC executives and a threat of a $1 billion lawsuit from Trump's legal team demanding a retraction and apology.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: YouTuber Candace Owens sparks TPUSA feud after hinting Charlie Kirk’s own mentors plotted his death claims Alex Clark
item.description: Turning Point USA host Alex Clark accused Candace Owens of implying Charlie Kirk's close associates were involved in his death. Clark stated Owens' claims, including questioning Tyler Robinson's guilt and suggesting "weird Fed messages," lacked proof and attacked Kirk's trusted circle. Owens' theories, like an underground tunnel escape, remain uncorroborated, dividing supporters.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: YouTube creator bans controversy: Why Enderman’s case has raised global concerns over AI-based moderation
item.description: YouTube's automated systems have sparked outrage after terminating numerous creator channels, including popular YouTuber Enderman's, without clear justification. Many creators reported sudden bans for "spam, scam, or deceptive practices" despite clean records. While some channels were restored after backlash, the incident highlights concerns over AI's unchecked power in content moderation and creator livelihoods.

item.title: Small plane carrying hurricane aid to Jamaica crashes into Florida pond minutes after takeoff; 'No victims found,' say authorities
item.description: A small plane carrying hurricane relief supplies to Jamaica crashed into a pond in Coral Springs shortly after taking off from Fort Lauderdale Executive Airport. Initial rescue efforts found no victims, and the operation has now transitioned to recovery. The aircraft was on a humanitarian mission to aid communities devastated by Hurricane Melissa.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kai Cenat’s girlfriend’s mom accuses daughter of ‘colorist’ views and brings up school race concerns
item.description: Twitch star Kai Cenat's girlfriend, Gigi Alayah, and her mother, Ashlee Monroe, are embroiled in renewed family drama. A new video shows Monroe discussing their strained relationship and making remarks about Gigi's past concerns regarding school demographics, sparking online debate about colorism and bias. Monroe also alluded to Gigi's fame and relationship with Cenat creating distance.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: $1 billion lawsuit or apology: Donald Trump warns BBC with ultimatum; sets deadline
item.description: Donald Trump is threatening the BBC with a $1 billion lawsuit over a Panorama documentary that he claims misrepresented his January 6th speech. His legal team alleges the broadcaster "fabricated" statements by editing his remarks out of context, demanding a retraction and apology by Friday. The controversy has already led to two senior BBC resignations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who was Michael Willis Heard? ‘Yes King’ TikToker passes away, daughter confirms heartbreaking news
item.description: Beloved TikTok creator and influencer Michael Willis Heard, known for his "Yes King" affirmations, has tragically passed away. His daughter confirmed the news, sharing the family's profound grief. Heard, a pastor and life coach, inspired thousands with his messages of positivity and self-empowerment, leaving a significant void in the online community.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Mariam Cisse cause of death: What happened to the Mali TikTok star during her livestream in Tonka
item.description: A young Malian TikTok star, Mariam Cisse, was brutally executed by extremists during a livestream in early November 2025. Known for her cheerful videos and support for the Malian army, her public killing in Tonka serves as a chilling warning. This incident highlights the escalating dangers for free expression online in northern Mali, where fear and violence are rampant.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Yes King dies: What led to the death of TikTok star Michael Willis?
item.description: TikTok sensation Michael Willis Heard, known as 'Yes King,' has passed away. His daughter confirmed the news, remembering him for his uplifting videos promoting self-love and confidence. The Elyria, Ohio native, who also served as a life coach and pastor-like figure, inspired millions with his positive energy. His sudden departure has deeply saddened his global fanbase.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: 'Wild': Australian senator says he just discovered 'Indian poop throwing festival'
item.description: After claiming that he came under vicious online attacks from tens of thousands of Indian who targeted his family, American influencer Tyler Oliveira released the documentary on Karnataka village Gorehabba or cow dung festival misrepresenting it as "poop festival". Now an Australian senator commented that it's crazy that he discovered this thing about India.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: BBC begins search for new director general after Tim Davie’s exit – who are the contenders?
item.description: The BBC faces a leadership vacuum as Tim Davie resigns after a doctored Trump speech controversy. Chair Samir Shah seeks a successor with newsroom and commercial acumen. Potential candidates include former Channel 4 chief Alex Mahon, ex-BBC content director Charlotte Moore, and Apple TV Plus executive Jay Hunt, among others, as the corporation navigates funding talks and shifting audience habits.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'My parents Christians, grandparents Sikh': Nikki Haley's son Nalin Haley says he was confused about religion
item.description: Nikki Haley's son Nalin Haley said Haley said he immersed himself in books on world religions to find out what he should follow when other kids of his age were reading about cars and dinosaurs. Eventually, he concluded that Christianity is the true faith but the conclusion was preceded by a spiritual experience that he did not detail in the interview.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kash Patel 'unpredictable, unreliable', broke promise to MI5 head, attended meeting in sweatshirt
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel faced scrutiny during a London visit, with reports detailing his unpredictable behavior and disregard for protocol. Incidents included a denied airport request, armed security issues, and an informal attire choice at a meeting. Patel also reportedly misled MI5 about an FBI agent's role and posed next to King Charles III for a photo, an NYT report claimed detailing Patel's missteps during his London visit earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Love won again': US Supreme Court rejects appeal seeking to overturn same-sex marriage rights
item.description: The Supreme Court declined to hear a case aiming to overturn same-sex marriage rights, upholding the 2015 ruling. This decision leaves the nationwide legality of gay marriage intact and preserves penalties for officials who refuse to issue licenses. LGBTQ advocates celebrated the outcome, emphasizing that public officials must serve all members of their communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Hadn't slept for two days before accident': Indian-origin woman jailed for 7 years for Georgia crash, was drunk and driving with suspended license
item.description: An Indian-origin woman, Sonal Nandkishor Patel, received a seven-year prison sentence for vehicular homicide and DUI. She caused a fatal crash on I-85 in Georgia, killing Omar Ortiz, a young father who had recently moved to the US. Patel was under the influence of alcohol and drugs, hadn't slept for days, and was driving with a suspended license.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
